subject: Linguistics
title: Internal Reconstruction
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Internal Reconstruction.

hook.text: Even without relatives, a language holds clues to its own past hidden inside its irregularities.

buildup.text: Internal reconstruction examines alternations within a single language to infer earlier stages.

discovery.text: English 'sing/sang/sung' reveals an older vowel alternation system—ablaut—that was once regular.

twist.text: This method works even for language isolates like Basque, which have no relatives to compare.

climax.text: Internal reconstruction is less powerful than the comparative method but reaches where comparison can't.

punchline.text: A language's past is written in its own irregularities.
